title: RunnerGatewayMessageV1
description: ADR-0008 §3 outbound runner gateway. The runner initiates every HTTPS request; the control plane never connects to a runner, so runners behind NAT work. Message bodies reuse remote-runner.v1 semantics unchanged (dispatch with a cmap1 permit bound to runner_id, adapter audience and envelope SHA256; dispatch_accepted / status / result / error; cancel); only the transport direction changes. POST /v1/gateway/claim long-polls for work (wait_seconds at most 50) and renews every lease listed in held_leases; the reply carries at most one assignment plus pending cancels, which the control plane can no longer push. POST /v1/gateway/reports carries one remote-runner.v1 reply for a lease and also renews it. A lease the control plane reports as expired enters the existing execution-uncertain path (task INPUT_REQUIRED, binding kept): it is never reassigned or rerun. Results are written to the ledger before the workflow is signalled. Artifacts are still recomputed by the control plane; runner-reported hashes are never trusted. Result artifacts are streamed (M09): before reporting a result the runner uploads each streamedArtifact's bytes with POST /v1/gateway/artifacts (artifactUpload), and the result report then carries only their metadata; reports with inline base64 artifacts from runners that predate streaming are still accepted. Authentication: every request carries requestAuthHeaders signed by the runner's enrolled Ed25519 key (runner-enrollment.v1); any failure, a revoked runner included, is one identical unsigned 401 error with code UNAUTHORIZED and nothing is executed or recorded. Every other reply carries responseAuthHeaders signed by the control-plane key the runner pinned at enrollment. Bodies never carry credentials, database addresses, provider stderr or tenant/owner identity: identity comes from the enrolled runner record, not from the request.

requestAuthHeaders.title: RunnerGatewayRequestAuthHeadersV1
requestAuthHeaders.description: HTTP headers on every runner request. Signature (base64url Ed25519 by the enrolled runner key) covers the UTF-8 string 'cmap-gateway-req1' LF METHOD LF path+query LF x-cmap-content-sha256 LF x-cmap-timestamp LF x-cmap-nonce LF x-cmap-runner-id. Timestamp skew at most 2 seconds; nonce single use inside the window. The domain prefix differs from remote-runner.v1 'cmap-runner-req1' so the two cannot be replayed into each other.

responseAuthHeaders.title: RunnerGatewayResponseAuthHeadersV1
responseAuthHeaders.description: HTTP header on every authenticated reply (errors included; only the 401 is unsigned). Signature (base64url Ed25519 by the control-plane key) covers 'cmap-gateway-res1' LF runner_id LF request x-cmap-nonce LF status code LF sha256 of the exact body bytes.

lease.title: RunnerGatewayLeaseV1
lease.description: Issued with an assignment and renewed by every claim or report that names it. Past expires_at the control plane stops waiting and records execution uncertain; it does not reassign.

claim.title: RunnerGatewayClaimV1
claim.description: POST /v1/gateway/claim. runner_id must equal x-cmap-runner-id. held_leases lists every lease the runner still executes (empty when idle); each is renewed. quota (optional, ADR-0009) is the runner's latest account-level quota snapshot for its wrapped agent, read by a zero-quota probe on the runner host and sent with the claim like remote-runner.v1 health.quota; the control plane keeps the newest one per runner for routing. Omitted when nothing could be read (older runners too): the control plane then treats the quota as unknown. It is advisory for routing only.

claimResult.title: RunnerGatewayClaimResultV1
claimResult.description: Reply to claim, sent when work or a cancel is available or wait_seconds elapsed. renewed: held leases still honored with their new expiry. expired: held leases the control plane already judged uncertain; the runner should stop them and must not report results for them. assignment: null, or one remote-runner.v1 dispatch with its new lease. cancels: remote-runner.v1 cancel messages for held leases.

report.title: RunnerGatewayReportV1
report.description: POST /v1/gateway/reports. body is exactly one remote-runner.v1 reply for the leased dispatch: dispatch_accepted (or a permit/admission error) right after verification, status on change, result once terminal. A result is persisted (artifacts recomputed) before the workflow is signalled.

reportAck.title: RunnerGatewayReportAckV1
reportAck.description: Reply to report. lease is the renewed lease, or null once the lease is closed (terminal report recorded).

artifactUpload.title: RunnerGatewayArtifactUploadV1
artifactUpload.description: Query of POST /v1/gateway/artifacts?lease_id=&sha256=&size= (metadata first; the raw artifact bytes are the request body, application/octet-stream). requestAuthHeaders sign path+query, so the declared sha256 and size are covered by the runner signature, and x-cmap-content-sha256 must equal sha256. Only for a lease this runner holds in state leased. The control plane streams the body into its content-addressed store, hashing as it writes; the upload is kept only if the bytes match both the declared sha256 and size, otherwise nothing is persisted and the reply is 422 EVIDENCE_HASH_MISMATCH (EVIDENCE_SECRET_DETECTED when the bytes match a known credential pattern). A declared size above the control plane cap is refused before reading with 413 EVIDENCE_FILE_TOO_LARGE. The kept upload is recorded under the lease: a result may only reference artifacts uploaded under its own lease.

uploadAck.title: RunnerGatewayUploadAckV1
uploadAck.description: Reply to an artifact upload: the bytes were recomputed and kept under the lease.

error.title: RunnerGatewayErrorV1
error.description: Gateway-level error. UNAUTHORIZED (HTTP 401, unsigned, identical for every authentication failure); LEASE_EXPIRED / LEASE_UNKNOWN for reports or uploads on a lease that is closed, expired or not held by this runner (no ledger write); INVALID_REQUEST for malformed or oversized bodies; EVIDENCE_HASH_MISMATCH / EVIDENCE_SECRET_DETECTED / EVIDENCE_FILE_TOO_LARGE for rejected artifact uploads (nothing persisted). No detail crosses the wire.
